title: Implement Transaction Purpose Field for AML Compliance
description: ShowTime PayHub is required to comply with a new Anti-Money Laundering (AML) regulation. This regulation mandates that all financial transactions must be associated with a 'purpose' string, provided by the initiator. This task involves updating the core payment service to include this new data point. The development will be split into two sessions: first, updating the data model and service logic; second, updating the unit tests to validate the new functionality.

project_spec.name: ShowTime PayHub
project_spec.description:
ShowTime PayHub is a medium-scale fintech banking platform designed in C that merges core banking functions with live entertainment experiences. The application lets users buy movie tickets, concert passes, in-game currency, and other digital media while seamlessly managing real-time payments, settlements, and compliance duties. Every transaction—whether topping up a gamer wallet, paying for a streaming subscription, or settling a backstage VIP upgrade—flows through a classic Model-View-Controller pipeline that keeps domain rules, UI layers, and orchestration logic strictly separated. 

Micro-services implement discrete capabilities such as Payment Processing, Fraud Detection, and Compliance Reporting, but the MVC pattern remains at the heart of each service: models hold business data (accounts, tickets, regulatory flags), controllers enforce workflows (transaction management, saga-based settlement), and views expose responses through REST/JSON or embedded WebSockets for streaming dashboards. By weaving interactive leaderboards, loyalty badges, and event-specific promotions directly into the banking flow, ShowTime PayHub makes financial operations feel like part of the show while maintaining regulatory rigor, audit trails, and Security-by-Design from end to end.
dependencies: libmicrohttpd (lightweight HTTP server for controller endpoints)
jansson (JSON parsing/serialization for model ↔ view data)
SQLite or PostgreSQL client libpq (persistence layer; audit logs, transactions)
libevent (non-blocking I/O for high-volume ticket purchase spikes)
RabbitMQ C client (AMQP for Saga Pattern orchestration across microservices)
libspf+libyara (rule engine foundations for fraud_detection service)
GLib/GObject (signal/slot MVC glue and entity collections)
CUnit or Check (unit testing of regulatory_compliance logic)
